subject: underground desert town
title: What If Your Whole Town Moved Underground? One in Australia Did

scenes.text: What if your town got so hot that everyone moved underground? In Coober Pedy, Australia, they did.
Summers often top 40 degrees Celsius; the record is 48. The ground is sandstone: soft enough to dig, strong enough to hold a roof.
In 1915 a teenager found opal here. Soldiers back from World War One dug their homes the way they'd dug trenches.
Today about half of the 1,500 residents live in dugouts. Inside stays around 23 to 24 degrees all year, no air conditioning needed.
There are underground churches, a hotel, a bookshop, a bar. The golf course has no grass, so they play at night with glowing balls.
The name is said to mean white man in a hole. Most of the world's gem opal still comes out of those holes.

description:
What if the surface got so hot that your whole town moved underground? In Coober Pedy, in the South Australian outback, about half the roughly 1,500 residents live in dugouts carved into sandstone, where the temperature stays around 23 to 24 degrees Celsius while summer days outside often pass 40.
Opal was found here in 1915, and returning World War One soldiers dug the first homes like trenches. The town now has underground churches, hotels and shops, more than 70 opal fields, and produces most of the world's gem-quality opal.

first_comment: Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome was filmed around Coober Pedy in 1985. Would you live in a house with no windows if it meant never needing air conditioning?
